podcast.title: The Rheostatics Active Periods and Reunions (1978-2007, 2015-Present)
podcast.body: The band had an initial run from 1978 to 2007, followed by a brief reunion. Since 2015, they have been performing occasional gigs together. "The Rio's initial run was from 78 to 2007. There was a brief reunion and since 2015 they played the occasional gig together."

podcast.title: The Rheostatics Formation and Influence (1978)
podcast.body: Formed in Toronto in 1978, The Rheostatics befriended The Tragically Hip in the 80s and 90s. Despite not being commercially focused, their unconventional and eclectic approach to rock garnered critical praise and significant influence. "Their history goes back to 1978 in Toronto. They became friends with the tragically hip through the 80s and 90s and they were never exactly commercial sounding but their unconventional and eclectic approach to rock made them beloved by critics and very influential in certain places."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Early Sound and Martin Tielli Joining (c. 1985)
podcast.body: Initially, The Rheostatics incorporated funk and R&B and featured a horn section. Around 1985, guitarist Martin Tielli joined, and the band evolved beyond its earlier sound, with these four members forming the core ever since. "the Rio's were into funk and R&B in the beginning and actually had a horn section but when they wanted to move beyond that guitarist Martin Tieli was brought in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Peak Period and Key Albums (1991-1997)
podcast.body: The band's most productive years were approximately from 1991 to 1997, during which they released notable albums such as *Melville*, *Whale Music*, and *Introducing Happiness*. "Their best years were from about 1991 through to maybe 1997, the period in which they released albums like Melville and Whale Music and Introducing Happiness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Decline and Hiatus (Pre-2006)
podcast.body: By 2006, the band's creative energy had waned, and members desired to pursue individual projects, preceding an eventual reunion. "But by 2006 all the magic had worn off and everybody wanted to do their own thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Another Roadside Attraction Tourmate
podcast.body: Rheostatics were Canadian performers who toured with The Tragically Hip's Another Roadside Attraction festival in 1993, 1995, and 1997. "Tourmates included Canadian performers like Daniel Landwass, Spirit of the West and the Rio Statics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Core Members and Lineup Stability
podcast.body: Guitarist and singer Dave Bidini and bassist Tim Vesley have been part of the band since its inception. Drummer Dave Clark joined within months of the band's founding and remained until the mid-1990s, contributing to the band's remarkable stability despite some lineup changes. "Guitarist and singer Dave Padini and bass player Tim Vesley have been part of the band from the beginning. Drummer Dave Clark goes back practically as far. He was there within a few months of the band's founding and stayed until the middle of the 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Dave Bidini's Diverse Career
podcast.body: Dave Bidini is a highly regarded writer of books and a newspaper columnist, frequently writing about hockey and music. He has authored "12 books," written plays, composed music for movies and TV, and currently serves as the editor of the *West End Phoenix*, a print newspaper in Toronto. "Dave Badini is the most visible. He's become a very well regarded writer of books in a newspaper columnist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Martin Tielli's Artistic Pursuits
podcast.body: Martin Tielli has become an accomplished painter, selling prints of his works, which have also been adapted for items like pillowcases. He has composed music for TV and film, and has released several solo albums. "Martin T. Ellie, he's become quite the painter and sells prints of his works. His paintings have also been adapted for other uses like pillowcases."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Post-Can Rock Revolution Breakup and Reform
podcast.body: Rheostatics were among the Canadian bands that broke up after the 1990s but later reformed due to public demand, demonstrating the lasting impact and fan loyalty cultivated during the Can Rock Revolution. "Others broke up, like I'm on the earth, and the real statics and lowest of the low, only to reform later due to public demand."

xref.title: Another Roadside Attraction Festival (1993)
xref.body: The Tragically Hip organized the festival "Another Roadside Attraction" in 1993, 1995, and 1997. This festival was one of several Canadian-based summer music events during the 90s, showcasing the growing strength and popularity of domestic music. "There was another roadside attraction, which was organized by the Trajically Hip in 1993, 1995 and 1997."
